evidence: For a standard normal variable Z the density is exp(-z^2/2)/sqrt(2 pi), normalized by the Gaussian integral. Set X=mu+sigma Z, sigma>0. The change-of-variable factor 1/sigma gives the displayed density. The mean of Z is zero by symmetry and its second moment is one by integration by parts, so X has mean mu and standard deviation sigma.
